info.title: masterly-hash
info.description: The masterly-hash .NET global tool: hash and verify passwords from a no-echo prompt or stdin, inspect and audit stored hashes, onion-wrap legacy hashes in a CSV export, benchmark the built-in profiles on this machine, check password policy (with an optional Have I Been Pwned k-anonymity lookup), and generate pepper keys and API keys.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: masterly-hash: hash, verify, inspect, audit and migrate password hashes with Masterly.Hash. Passwords are read from a no-echo prompt or --stdin, never from arguments.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

commands.name: hash
commands.description: Hash a password from a no-echo prompt (asked twice) or --stdin, and print the hash.

options.name: --profile
options.description: Built-in profile for the new hash. Default: 2026a (Argon2id, 64 MiB, t=3).

options.name: --stdin
options.description: Read the password from the first line of standard input instead of prompting. [default: False]

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify a password from a no-echo prompt or --stdin against a stored hash. Exit code 0 = match, 1 = mismatch, 2 = error.

options.name: --stdin
options.description: Read the password from the first line of standard input instead of prompting. [default: False]

arguments.name: STOREDHASH
arguments.description: The stored hash (Masterly or any supported legacy format). Quote it: it contains '$'.

commands.name: inspect
commands.description: Describe a stored hash: format, profile, pepper key, onion-wrapping and whether a login would rehash it.

options.name: --pepper-key-ids
options.description: Comma-separated pepper key ids your application knows, current key first (e.g. k2,k1). Peppered hashes ($mh$p=...,k=ID$...) are then classified instead of reported as unknown. Only the ids are needed, never the keys.

arguments.name: STOREDHASH
arguments.description: The stored hash to describe. Quote it: it contains '$'.

commands.name: audit
commands.description: Audit stored hashes (every legacy format is recognized): formats, profiles, weak, needs-rehash and duplicate counts. Reads one hash per line, or one CSV column.

options.name: --column
options.description: Read the hash from this 1-based CSV column instead of taking whole lines.

options.name: --delimiter
options.description: CSV field delimiter: one character, or 'tab'. [default: ,]

options.name: --header
options.description: Skip the first line/record (a header row). [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Report format. [default: markdown]

options.name: --pepper-key-ids
options.description: Comma-separated pepper key ids your application knows, current key first (e.g. k2,k1). Peppered hashes ($mh$p=...,k=ID$...) are then classified instead of reported as unknown. Only the ids are needed, never the keys.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: File with one stored hash per line (or a CSV with --column); '-' reads standard input.

commands.name: wrap
commands.description: Onion-wrap legacy hashes in one CSV column (Argon2id over the legacy digest), streaming. Other columns are kept; wrapped hashes verify with the original passwords and upgrade on the next login.

options.name: --column
options.description: 1-based column that holds the stored hash.

options.name: --delimiter
options.description: CSV field delimiter: one character, or 'tab'. [default: ,]

options.name: --header
options.description: The first record is a header row; copy it unchanged. [default: False]

options.name: --v1-algorithm
options.description: Digest of Masterly.Hash 1.x hashes in this file. 1.x did not record it, so v1 hashes are only wrapped when it is given.

options.name: --profile
options.description: Profile for the wrapping hash. Default: 2026a.

options.name: --weak-only
options.description: Only wrap weak hashes (unsalted digests, 1.x, phpass, low-cost bcrypt/PBKDF2); copy the rest unchanged. [default: False]

options.name: --force
options.description: Overwrite the output file if it exists. [default: False]

options.name: --parallelism
options.description: Hashes computed at once. Each Argon2id hash uses the profile's memory (64 MiB for 2026a). [default: 4]

options.name: --pepper-key-ids
options.description: Comma-separated pepper key ids your application knows, current key first (e.g. k2,k1). Peppered hashes ($mh$p=...,k=ID$...) are then classified instead of reported as unknown. Only the ids are needed, never the keys.

arguments.name: INPUT.CSV
arguments.description: CSV export of the password table.

arguments.name: OUTPUT.CSV
arguments.description: Where to write the CSV with wrapped hashes. Written to a temporary file and renamed on success.

commands.name: bench
commands.description: Time each built-in profile on this machine (median of 5 runs) and recommend Server2026a or Constrained2026a.

options.name: --target-ms
options.description: Longest acceptable time for one hash on this machine, in milliseconds. [default: 250]

commands.name: policy
commands.description: Check a password from a no-echo prompt or --stdin against the NIST SP 800-63B policy: score, crack-time estimates, violations and suggestions. Exit code 0 = acceptable, 1 = rejected, 2 = error (including --pwned when the breach check is unavailable).

options.name: --stdin
options.description: Read the password from the first line of standard input instead of prompting. [default: False]

options.name: --min-length
options.description: Minimum length in code points (8-128). Default 15, the NIST minimum for a single-factor password.

options.name: --pwned
options.description: ONLINE: also look the password up in Have I Been Pwned. Only the first 5 hex characters of its SHA-1 hash are sent (k-anonymity). [default: False]

options.name: --allow-unavailable
options.description: With --pwned: if Have I Been Pwned cannot be reached, judge the password without it (exit 0/1) instead of failing with exit code 2. [default: False]

options.name: --user-name
options.description: The account's user name; passwords containing it are rejected.

options.name: --email
options.description: The account's email address; passwords containing its parts are rejected.

commands.name: generate
commands.description: Print a new random 32-byte pepper key, base64-encoded, for HmacPepper.

commands.name: generate
commands.description: Print a new API key and its lookup hash (HMAC-SHA256). Without --key-env or --key-stdin a new lookup key is generated and printed.

options.name: --prefix
options.description: Key prefix, e.g. mh_live: 1-32 ASCII letters, digits and single underscores, starting with a letter.

options.name: --key-id
options.description: Id of the HMAC lookup key, stored in the lookup hash. [default: k1]

options.name: --key-env
options.description: Read the base64 HMAC lookup key (32+ bytes) from this environment variable instead of generating one.

options.name: --key-stdin
options.description: Read the base64 HMAC lookup key from the first line of standard input instead of generating one. [default: False]

options.name: --entropy-bytes
options.description: Random bytes in the key (16-64). [default: 32]
